featured.title: Deadly Boat Disaster In Nigeria's Sokoto State
featured.content: An overloaded boat capsized in northwestern Nigeria's Sokoto State while carrying farmers and labourers. Reports say at least 40 people have died, with many of the victims believed to be children. Other reports put the death toll at around 50. Rescue and recovery operations are continuing as authorities work to establish the final number of victims.

articles.title: Sokoto Boat Disaster Leaves Dozens Dead
articles.description: An overloaded boat capsized in Goronyo Local Government Area of Sokoto State. At least 40 people have reportedly died, while some reports put the toll at about 50. Many victims were children travelling with farmers and labourers. Rescue and recovery efforts are continuing.

articles.title: Nigeria Faces Renewed Focus On Waterway Safety
articles.description: The Sokoto tragedy has renewed concerns about overloaded boats, passenger safety and emergency response on Nigerian waterways. Authorities and communities continue efforts to improve safety and reduce the risk of similar disasters.

articles.title: Two UN Staff Members Released In Afghanistan
articles.description: Two Afghan national staff members working with the UN mission in Afghanistan were released on Thursday after being detained in Herat since August 9. The United Nations said the two men were released in good health.

articles.title: Serbia Turns To Russia For Wildfire Assistance
articles.description: Serbia has sought Russian help to fight major wildfires after difficulties securing enough firefighting aircraft from European partners. A Russian IL-76 firefighting aircraft arrived in Serbia and began supporting the response.

articles.title: Europe Continues Fighting Major Wildfires
articles.description: Wildfires remain a serious concern across parts of Europe, including Serbia, France, Greece, Spain, Italy and other countries. Extreme heat, dry conditions and limited firefighting resources are complicating emergency responses.

articles.title: France Continues Monitoring Wildfire Damage
articles.description: French authorities continue to deal with the effects of a difficult wildfire season. A fire in the southwestern Landes region recently forced the evacuation of 525 people after flames spread through pine woodland.

articles.title: Russian Strikes Hit Ukraine
articles.description: Russia carried out major air attacks on Ukraine, with Kyiv and surrounding areas among the areas affected. Ukrainian officials reported significant casualties and damage while continuing to call for stronger air-defence support.

articles.title: Ukraine War Remains A Major Security Concern
articles.description: The war between Russia and Ukraine continues to shape European security policy. European governments remain focused on military assistance, sanctions, air defence and diplomatic efforts while attacks continue.

articles.title: US Dollar Heads Toward Weekly Loss
articles.description: The US dollar is heading toward a weekly decline and remains near multi-month lows as investors assess concerns about US debt, Treasury-market stability and economic policy. Bond-market pressures remain an important issue for global investors.

articles.title: US Debt And Bond Markets Remain Under Scrutiny
articles.description: Investors continue watching America's large budget deficit, rising government debt and Treasury yields. Recent market volatility has raised questions about the long-term cost of government borrowing and confidence in fiscal policy.

articles.title: Teen Withdraws Social-Media Lawsuit
articles.description: A 15-year-old New Jersey girl has voluntarily withdrawn a lawsuit against Meta, Google and Snap ahead of trial. The case accused the companies of designing platforms that contributed to social-media addiction and harm to young users. The companies deny the allegations.

articles.title: Social Media Safety Debate Continues
articles.description: The withdrawal of the New Jersey case does not end the wider legal debate surrounding social-media platforms and young users. Thousands of related claims involving technology companies remain part of ongoing litigation in the United States.

articles.title: US And South Korea Scale Back Military Exercises
articles.description: The United States and South Korea have agreed to shorten their annual joint military exercises from 11 days to five and reduce their scope. North Korea has criticised the exercises, while Seoul and Washington describe the training as defensive.

articles.title: Korean Peninsula Security Remains In Focus
articles.description: Changes to US-South Korea military exercises come amid continued security concerns on the Korean Peninsula. Washington and Seoul are balancing military readiness with efforts to manage tensions with North Korea.

articles.title: Global Markets Face Pressure From Oil And Bond Yields
articles.description: Global financial markets remain sensitive to high oil prices, elevated government bond yields and geopolitical uncertainty. Investors are assessing the potential effects of energy costs on inflation and economic growth.

articles.title: Oil Prices Remain Elevated
articles.description: Oil markets remain under pressure as the continuing US-Iran conflict affects supply expectations and shipping through the Gulf region. Traders are watching developments around the Strait of Hormuz for signs of further disruption.

articles.title: Asian Markets Head Toward A Difficult Week
articles.description: Most Asian stock markets were heading toward weekly losses as global bond yields and oil prices remained elevated. Investors are also assessing concerns about inflation, government debt and geopolitical uncertainty.

articles.title: AI Investment Remains A Major Global Trend
articles.description: Artificial intelligence continues attracting large amounts of investment in computing infrastructure, chips and data centres. Investors are increasingly debating whether the scale of AI spending can generate sufficient long-term economic returns.

articles.title: Robotics Industry Moves Toward An AI Breakthrough
articles.description: Chinese robotics company Unitree says the industry may be approaching a major breakthrough in embodied artificial intelligence. The company believes future robots could eventually perform a much wider range of tasks using voice and text instructions.

articles.title: Brazil Launches Major AI Supercomputer Investment
articles.description: Brazil has announced a major investment of roughly 2.3 billion reais to strengthen its artificial-intelligence capabilities. Projects involve both Chinese and US technology partners as Brazil seeks greater technological capacity and strategic independence.

articles.title: Nigeria's Economic Outlook Remains A Major Election Issue
articles.description: Nigeria's economy continues to face pressure from living costs, employment challenges and security concerns as the country moves deeper into the election period. Recent inflation data showed headline inflation at 15.43 percent in July.

articles.title: International Security Remains A Major Concern
articles.description: Wars, military tensions, energy disruptions and political uncertainty continue affecting governments and markets around the world. Diplomacy remains central to efforts aimed at preventing further escalation.

articles.title: Today's Big Question
articles.description: When governments face disasters, economic pressure and security challenges at the same time, should their first priority be protecting lives, stabilising the economy, or strengthening national security? What do you think?

articles.title: Quote Of The Day
articles.description: Progress begins when we stop waiting for perfect conditions and start making responsible choices with what we have.
